section_summary: This section contains State Department despatches, memoranda, correspondence, and informational materials from 1948 and 1949 concerning Japanese higher education and postwar educational reforms under the Allied Occupation. A major portion documents the establishment and fundraising campaign for the International Christian University in Japan, headed by former Ambassador Joseph C. Grew and Dr. Ralph Diffendorfer, with discussions focusing on academic standards, democratic values, and measures to prevent Communist infiltration. Additionally, the file includes a 1948 memorandum of conversation with Tokyo University President Shigeru Nambara regarding university reorganization, as well as inquiries regarding the credentials of Ibaraki Christian College.

subfiles.about: Transmits a memorandum of conversation with Shigeru Nambara and Seijiro Yoshizawa concerning university decentralization, junior colleges, teachers unions, and governmental reorganization.
subfiles.from: W. J. Sebald, Acting Political Adviser, Office of the United States Political Adviser for Japan, Tokyo
subfiles.summary: Transmits a summary and memorandum of a December 27, 1947 conversation with Shigeru Nambara and Seijiro Yoshizawa discussing Japanese educational reform, university decentralization, teachers unions, and Central Liaison Office reorganization.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 43: Transmittal of a Memorandum of Conversation With Mr. NAMBARA, Shigeru, President of Tokyo University, and Mr. YOSHIZAWA, Seijiro, Vice President of the Central Liaison Office
subfiles.to: The Secretary of State, Washington

subfiles.about: Records discussions at a dinner meeting with Shigeru Nambara and Seijiro Yoshizawa regarding university reforms, international exchanges, teachers unions, and Japanese diplomatic reorganization.
subfiles.from: W. Henry Lawrence, Jr., Second Secretary, and Rolland H. Bushner, Third Secretary
subfiles.summary: Tokyo University President Shigeru Nambara argued against adopting the American junior college system and opposed decentralizing national universities into prefectural institutions due to financial constraints and teacher shortages. He expressed concern over elementary teachers union radicalism and urged the resumption of sending young Japanese professors and students to England and America. Central Liaison Office Vice President Seijiro Yoshizawa discussed the planned dissolution of his agency, diplomatic training needs, and dismissed rumors of Japanese diplomatic opposition to United Nations trusteeship.
subfiles.title: Enclosure No. 1 to Despatch No. 43: Memorandum of Conversation on Decentralization of Japanese Universities, International Exchange of Teachers and Students, Reorganization of the Central Liaison Office and the Ministry of Foreign Affairs
subfiles.to: Office of the United States Political Adviser for Japan

subfiles.about: Reports on remarks by Naotake Sato and Ken Harada regarding United Nations trusteeship and the newly formed United Nations Association of Japan.
subfiles.from: Russell Brines, Chief of Tokyo AP Bureau (Pacific Stars and Stripes)
subfiles.summary: Article reporting that Naotake Sato and Ken Harada considered UN trusteeship over Japan unsuitable during a press conference for the United Nations Association.
subfiles.title: Attachment to Enclosure No. 1: Nippon Diplomats Disapprove UN Japan Trusteeship
subfiles.to: Readers of Pacific Stars and Stripes

subfiles.about: Announces the elimination of the Central Liaison Office effective February 1, 1948, and the redistribution of its liaison functions.
subfiles.from: General Headquarters, Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers
subfiles.summary: Announces the dissolution of the Central Liaison Office and redistribution of its functions effective February 1, 1948.
subfiles.title: Enclosure No. 2 to Despatch No. 43: Dissolution of Japanese Central Liaison Office (Excerpt from Daily Bulletin No. 9, GHQ, SCAP)
subfiles.to: Allied Occupation Personnel

subfiles.about: Presents an outline of the project to establish an International Christian University in Japan and requests the State Department's approval.
subfiles.from: John Coventry Smith, Vice President, Japan Christian University Foundation
subfiles.summary: Presents plans for a Protestant-sponsored Christian university in Japan, starting with a Graduate School of Teaching, and requests State Department endorsement.
subfiles.title: Letter from Japan Christian University Foundation to Secretary of State Dean Acheson
subfiles.to: Dean G. Acheson, Secretary of State

subfiles.about: Provides a detailed briefing on the background, educational philosophy, structure, campus, and financial plans for establishing an International Christian University in Japan.
subfiles.from: The Japan Christian University Foundation, Inc.
subfiles.summary: This briefing statement details the proposal by ten North American Protestant denominations to establish an International Christian University near Tokyo to advance democratic education and counter Communist ideology. The institution plans a 350-acre campus and will initially establish a graduate school of education to train secondary and college teachers in modern pedagogy and individual freedom. It outlines a ten-million-dollar fundraising objective in the United States and Canada alongside funds pledged by Japanese donors.
subfiles.title: A Briefing Statement: A Christian University for Japan
subfiles.to: General Public and Prospective Supporters

subfiles.about: Clarifies that the Department had indeed answered previous correspondence regarding the proposed graduate school in Japan after initial confusion.
subfiles.from: J. Robert Schaetzel, Office of International Trade Policy (ITP)
subfiles.summary: Reports that the Department had already answered the graduate school inquiry, resolving confusion caused by vacation schedules.
subfiles.title: Office Memorandum: Letter to the Secretary of State with respect to a Proposal to establish a Graduate School in Japan
subfiles.to: Livingston T. Merchant (FE) and Howland H. Sargeant (P)

subfiles.about: Notes that neither OII nor DCR had records of the incoming letter, which was located in POS/J.
subfiles.from: F. [Frank A. Schuler, Jr.]
subfiles.summary: Notes that the missing correspondence was located in POS/J after search across Department divisions.
subfiles.title: File Note on Missing Correspondence in POS/J
subfiles.to: File

subfiles.about: Informs Brown that his earlier letter regarding the graduate school campaign could not be found and suggests submitting a duplicate.
subfiles.from: J. Robert Schaetzel, Special Assistant to the Director, Office of International Trade Policy
subfiles.summary: Informs Brown that his letter regarding the graduate school project was misplaced in the Department and requests a duplicate.
subfiles.title: Letter from J. Robert Schaetzel to John Crosby Brown
subfiles.to: John Crosby Brown, Care of Tamblyn and Brown

subfiles.about: Acknowledges the foundation's June 29 letter, expresses sympathy with its objectives, and refers Smith to Frank A. Schuler, Jr. for discussion.
subfiles.from: George V. Allen, Assistant Secretary of State (For the Secretary of State)
subfiles.summary: Acknowledges Smith's letter, endorses the spiritual aims of the university project, and arranges a meeting with Frank A. Schuler, Jr.
subfiles.title: Letter from Assistant Secretary George V. Allen to Rev. John C. Smith
subfiles.to: The Reverend John C. Smith, D.D., Vice President, Japan Christian University Foundation

subfiles.about: Records that John C. Smith's June 29 correspondence is held in Mr. Schuler's office pending Smith's arrival.
subfiles.from: R. Kelly, POS
subfiles.summary: Records that June 29 correspondence from Mr. Smith is held in Schuler's office pending his arrival.
subfiles.title: Handwritten File Note on Smith Correspondence
subfiles.to: File

subfiles.about: Official Department file copy of the July 21, 1949 letter endorsing the Japan Christian University project.
subfiles.from: George V. Allen, Assistant Secretary of State
subfiles.summary: Official classified file copy of Assistant Secretary Allen's July 21, 1949 letter to Reverend John C. Smith.
subfiles.title: Official File Copy: Letter from George V. Allen to Rev. John C. Smith
subfiles.to: The Reverend John C. Smith, D.D., Vice President, Japan Christian University Foundation

subfiles.about: Recommends supporting the International Christian University in Japan and suggests points for replying to Joseph C. Grew.
subfiles.from: Marshall Green, Office of Northeast Asian Affairs (NA)
subfiles.summary: Recommends supporting the International Christian University, noting that concerns over monopolizing educators have subsided, and advises on replying to Grew.
subfiles.title: Office Memorandum: Support for International Christian University in Japan
subfiles.to: W. Walton Butterworth, Assistant Secretary for Far Eastern Affairs (FE)

subfiles.about: Transmits compiled notes and correspondence regarding the International Christian University project and invites State Department guidance.
subfiles.from: Joseph C. Grew
subfiles.summary: Explains his acceptance of the campaign chairmanship for the International Christian University, enclosing notes and correspondence, and inviting feedback.
subfiles.title: Letter from Joseph C. Grew to Assistant Secretary W. Walton Butterworth
subfiles.to: W. Walton Butterworth, Assistant Secretary of State

subfiles.about: Compiles correspondence, statements, and notes documenting policy discussions, fundraising plans, anti-communist concerns, and high-level endorsements for the International Christian University.
subfiles.from: Joseph C. Grew
subfiles.summary: This compilation assembles letters, memoranda, press releases, and statements detailing Joseph C. Grew's involvement as National Chairman for the International Christian University fund drive. It includes diplomatic reports from Tokyo, correspondence with State Department officials, foundation leaders Ralph Diffendorfer and James L. Fieser, campaign director John Crosby Brown, and Japanese figures including Prime Minister Shigeru Yoshida, Princess Chichibu, and Professor Yasaka Takagi. The materials emphasize establishing top-tier non-sectarian academic standards, teaching democratic principles by example rather than narrow proselytization, and preventing Communist infiltration.
subfiles.title: Enclosure: Notes and Correspondence Relating to the International Christian University in Japan, 1949
subfiles.to: W. Walton Butterworth, Department of State

subfiles.about: Requests information about an educational institution mentioned in an attached inquiry letter.
subfiles.from: Mrs. Smith, Division of Public Liaison (PL)
subfiles.summary: Requests information from research files regarding Ibaraki Christian College to reply to a public inquiry.
subfiles.title: Form DS-10 Reference Slip: Inquiry Regarding Ibaraki Christian College
subfiles.to: Division of Research for Far East (DRF)

subfiles.about: States there is no information in DRF files regarding the college and suggests writing to SCAP's Religious and Cultural Resources Division.
subfiles.from: William G. Jones, DRF-NEA Economics
subfiles.summary: Reports no departmental files on Ibaraki Christian College and suggests directing the inquirer to SCAP in Tokyo.
subfiles.title: Form DS-10 Reference Slip: Response Regarding Ibaraki Christian College
subfiles.to: Mrs. Smith, Division of Public Liaison (PL)

subfiles.about: Inquires about the status and standing of Ibaraki Christian College before granting permission to translate a book by her late brother Lewis Browne.
subfiles.from: Rebecca Browne Tarlow
subfiles.summary: Requests background and accreditation information on Ibaraki Christian College before permitting Japanese translation of her late brother Lewis Browne's book.
subfiles.title: Letter from Rebecca Browne Tarlow Requesting Information on Ibaraki Christian College
subfiles.to: Department of State

subfiles.about: States the Department lacks information on Ibaraki Christian College and suggests alternative contacts at SCAP and mission organizations.
subfiles.from: Leonard R. Cowles, Chief, Public Views and Inquiries Section, Division of Public Liaison (For the Secretary of State)
subfiles.summary: Advises that the Department lacks information on Ibaraki Christian College and suggests contacting SCAP and mission organizations.
subfiles.title: Letter from Leonard R. Cowles to Rebecca Browne Tarlow
subfiles.to: Mrs. Rebecca Browne Tarlow

subfiles.about: Encloses correspondence with Ralph Diffendorfer regarding a committee chaired by Vice Admiral Neil Philips to screen university appointments.
subfiles.from: Joseph C. Grew
subfiles.summary: Encloses correspondence with Ralph Diffendorfer and announces Vice Admiral Neil Philips's acceptance to chair an advisory screening committee for university personnel.
subfiles.title: Letter from Joseph C. Grew to Assistant Secretary W. Walton Butterworth Regarding Faculty Screening
subfiles.to: W. Walton Butterworth, Assistant Secretary of State

subfiles.about: Outlines core principles for the university, warns against Communist infiltration, and proposes an independent screening committee for non-Japanese faculty and staff.
subfiles.from: Joseph C. Grew
subfiles.summary: Urges rigorous selection of faculty to prevent Communist infiltration in Japan and recommends creating an independent advisory committee to screen appointees through security agencies.
subfiles.title: Enclosure: Letter from Joseph C. Grew to Dr. Ralph E. Diffendorfer
subfiles.to: Dr. Ralph E. Diffendorfer, President, Japan International Christian University Foundation

subfiles.about: Agrees with Grew on barring Communist influence and explains that the foundation's Personnel Committee will establish the advisory screening committee.
subfiles.from: Ralph E. Diffendorfer, President, Japan International Christian University Foundation
subfiles.summary: Diffendorfer agrees that faculty must reject communism and notes that the Personnel Committee will establish the requested advisory committee with Vice Admiral Philips.
subfiles.title: Enclosure: Letter from Dr. Ralph E. Diffendorfer to Joseph C. Grew
subfiles.to: Joseph C. Grew

subfiles.about: Urges an immediate reply to her November 13 inquiry concerning Ibaraki Christian College so she can decide on translation rights for 'The Graphic Bible'.
subfiles.from: Rebecca Browne Tarlow
subfiles.summary: Follows up urgently on her previous inquiry regarding Ibaraki Christian College's credentials to authorize translation of 'The Graphic Bible'.
subfiles.title: Follow-up Letter from Rebecca Browne Tarlow Requesting Information on Ibaraki Christian College
subfiles.to: Department of State

subfiles.about: Enclosed copy of Tarlow's November 13, 1949 letter inquiring about Ibaraki Christian College.
subfiles.from: Rebecca Browne Tarlow
subfiles.summary: Enclosed copy of Tarlow's original November 13, 1949 letter requesting background information on Ibaraki Christian College.
subfiles.title: Enclosure: Copy of Letter of November 13, 1949 from Rebecca Browne Tarlow
subfiles.to: Department of State
